name: TeraWulf
founded: 2021 (Delaware; Beowulf Energy lineage to 1990; Lake Mariner operations from March 2022)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: TeraWulf has converted itself from a bitcoin miner into an AI-campus landlord faster than any peer — 839 MW of leased critical IT and ~$27B+ of contracted revenue as of the Q2 2026 deck, anchored by the 401 MW / 20-year / ~$19B Anthropic lease at Hawesville, KY (July 2026, ~$33B with extensions) on top of 378 MW of Fluidstack leases at Lake Mariner carrying $3.2B of Google credit backstops — credit support Google bought with warrants now equal to ~14% of the company pro forma. Those same warrants produce the GAAP distortion that defines the stock: a $939.9M Q2 2026 net loss, $755.7M of it a non-cash warrant mark-to-market, which the market shrugged off (shares fell under 1% on the print, +47% YTD at the time). BACKGROUND: Easton, MD; incorporated 2021 out of Paul Prager's Beowulf Energy lineage (1990). Flagship Lake Mariner campus sits on the former 700 MW Somerset coal plant on Lake Ontario (NYISO Zone A, ~90% zero-carbon grid, 90 MW NYPA allocation); the platform now spans five brownfield campuses totaling 3,630 MW gross / 2,921 MW critical IT. Legacy mining (~9.3 EH/s, 245 MW) is down to ~29% of revenue and shrinking. Per MarketBeat, six consecutive EPS misses — while the Street holds a Strong Buy consensus at roughly 2.3x the share price: the market prices contracted backlog, not the P&L.
ecosystemRole: We assess TeraWulf as the cleanest test of the 'power landlord of AI' model (Bernstein's framing, June 2026): it monetizes brownfield power sites — energized substations, existing interconnects, cheap zero-carbon supply — into 10–20-year take-or-pay leases with AI tenants whose own credit is thin, papered over by investment-grade support (Google's ~$4.5B of backstops across the Fluidstack chain; Anthropic's lease with investment-grade credit support). For this ecosystem's power-chain vendors, TeraWulf is a live buildout: CB-series liquid-cooled buildings at Lake Mariner at ~$9.1M per critical-IT MW, 336 MW under construction, and Data Center Frontier flags long-lead electrical equipment — transformers, switchgear, chillers — as the choke point on the Anthropic schedule. Basis: company disclosures and independent trade coverage; the equity story (warrant dilution, related-party history) is separable from the vendor read-through.

productsAndServices.name: HPC/AI colocation leasing (WULF Compute)
productsAndServices.description: Build-to-suit, Tier III-aligned AI data-center leases of 10–20 years with annual escalators: Fluidstack at 378 MW critical IT across Lake Mariner's CB-3/CB-4/CB-5 (~$6.7B contracted, up to ~$16B with extensions, Google-backstopped), Anthropic at 401 MW at the Justified campus in Hawesville, KY (20 years, ~$19B initial term, ~$33B with two 5-year extensions), and Core42/G42 at 60 MW (delivered Jul 2025–Mar 2026, ~$1.1B over 10 years). Target ~85% site-NOI margin; build cost guided $8–10M per critical-IT MW ($9.1M actual at Lake Mariner in Q2 2026).
highlights: 839 MW leased critical IT; ~$27B+ contracted revenue; ~$1.5B average annual NOI (Q2 2026 deck)
Google credit support totals $3.2B at Lake Mariner (plus $1.3B at the exited Abernathy JV) in exchange for warrants — ~73.5M shares at $0.01, ~14% pro forma
102 MW energized at Lake Mariner as of July 2026; 438 contracted MW targeted energized by 1H 2027
productsAndServices.positioning: Leads the miner-pivot cohort on contracted backlog ($12.8B at YE2025 before the $19B Anthropic add) vs Core Scientific ~$10.2B, Applied Digital ~$11B, Cipher ~$9.3B, IREN's $9.7B Microsoft deal; Bernstein tags WULF and Cipher the 'power landlords of AI'.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term triple/modified-gross leases to AI clouds and labs; project-level debt (WULF Compute LLC $3.2B 7.75% notes) secured by the leases.
targetSegments: Target: 250–500 MW of new contracted capacity per year
productsAndServices.roadmap: CB-4 first-hall revenue late Sep 2026, CB-5 first hall early 2027; Anthropic capacity 2H 2027 → full 401 MW early 2028.

productsAndServices.name: Brownfield power-campus platform (five sites)
productsAndServices.description: The underlying asset base: former coal/smelter industrial sites with energized substations and existing high-voltage interconnects. Lake Mariner, Barker NY (600 MW critical IT design; ~500 MW grid interconnection expandable toward 750 MW; 90 MW NYPA allocation); Justified, Hawesville KY (former Century Aluminum smelter, ~480 MW, acquired Feb 2026 for ~$302M total consideration); Muskie, eastern KY (1+ GW gross, acquired May 2026, AEP building a 345 kV substation off the 765 kV network); Lake Hawkeye/Cayuga, Lansing NY (80-year ground lease, ~320 MW critical IT potential, 138 MW of sub-5¢/kWh power expected 2H 2026, planned 67 MW solar + 800 MWh BESS); Chesapeake, Morgantown MD (pending close, FERC-approved — 'Bring Your Own Generation' net-generator design: Phase I 500 MW generation + 250 MW battery + 500 MW data-center load).
highlights: Platform totals 3,630 MW gross / 2,921 MW critical IT — 839 MW contracted + ~2.1 GW pipeline
Brownfield thesis: the substation and interconnect, not the building, are the scarce asset
~90% zero-carbon grid supply at the NY sites (NYISO Zone A) — contested by short-sellers over REC accounting
productsAndServices.positioning: Power-first identity ('Power is the constraint. We control it.') against greenfield developers waiting in interconnection queues; the Abernathy TX JV exit (~$530M, ~20% IRR, July 2026) showed the platform can also recycle capital out of non-core geographies.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Owned or long-term ground-leased sites; capacity leased through WULF Compute.
targetSegments: AI tenants needing 100 MW+ blocks on 2027–2030 timelines
productsAndServices.roadmap: Muskie initial 500 MW ramp Q4 2028 (+500 MW ~2030); Lake Hawkeye operations ~2029; Chesapeake ~2030.

productsAndServices.name: Bitcoin self-mining (legacy, shrinking)
productsAndServices.description: ~49,400 miners / ~9.3 EH/s at YE2025 across 245 MW of legacy capacity at Lake Mariner. Digital-asset revenue fell from $47.6M in Q2 2025 to $12.8M in Q2 2026 (~29% of revenue) as buildings and power are progressively redeployed to HPC. The nuclear-powered Nautilus JV (Talen, 2¢/kWh) was exited in Oct 2024 at ~$92M / 3.4x MOIC to fund the first HPC buildings.
highlights: Mining is now the bridge business funding nothing — HPC leases carry the story
No stated exit date; capacity converts as HPC demand claims the megawatts
productsAndServices.positioning: Among miner-pivots, TeraWulf is furthest along in revenue mix: HPC hit 71% of revenue in Q2 2026 — first of the cohort to cross majority-HPC.
targetSegments: Opportunistic BTC production on already-owned power
productsAndServices.roadmap: Progressive conversion; no committed fleet refresh disclosed since the 2024 S21 Pro upgrade plan.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q2 2026: revenue $44.8M with HPC leasing at $31.9M (71% of revenue, +52% QoQ); GAAP net loss $939.9M — $755.7M of it the non-cash Google-warrant mark-to-market; cash $3.0B; stock fell <1%
recentDevelopments.read: The quarter that proved the mix shift is real and that GAAP optics will stay broken while the stock rises — every rally marks the warrants up through the P&L.

recentDevelopments.headline: Anthropic signs a 20-year, 401 MW lease at the Justified campus (Hawesville, KY) — ~$19B initial term, ~$33B with extensions, investment-grade credit support; same day, TeraWulf exits the Abernathy TX JV to Fluidstack for ~$530M (~20% IRR)
recentDevelopments.read: Graduation day: from middleman tenancy (Fluidstack) to a direct frontier-lab lease, while recycling the one non-core-geography asset into wholly-owned Kentucky. The Anthropic-behind-Fluidstack chain that trade press mapped in Nov 2025 became explicit.

recentDevelopments.headline: Acquires 1+ GW eastern Kentucky campus ('Muskie', EastPark Industrial Park, ~$231M) — Kentucky Power (AEP) building a 345 kV substation off the 765 kV network; initial 500 MW ramp targeted Q4 2028
recentDevelopments.read: The pipeline replenishment move: with Lake Mariner effectively sold out, the next gigawatt has to come from new brownfields.

recentDevelopments.headline: Closes ~$1.04B common stock offering at $19.00/share (Morgan Stanley lead) for Hawesville construction and bridge repayment
recentDevelopments.read: Equity issued at 6x the 2024 lows — the dilution machine keeps running, but at progressively better prices.

recentDevelopments.headline: FY2025: revenue $168.5M (mining $151.6M / HPC $16.9M), net loss $661.4M, cash $3.7B after raising $6.5B+ of capital during 2025; 522 MW contracted, $12.8B+ backlog
recentDevelopments.read: The transition year on paper: nearly all revenue still mining, nearly all value contracted HPC — the gap the 2026-27 energization schedule has to close.

recentDevelopments.headline: Acquires the Hawesville, KY brownfield (former Century Aluminum smelter, ~480 MW — becomes Justified Data) and agrees to buy the Morgantown, MD generating station (becomes Chesapeake Data & Energy, 'bring your own generation' design)
recentDevelopments.read: Two coal/smelter-legacy sites in one release — the brownfield playbook applied beyond New York, one grid-powered, one net-generator.

recentDevelopments.headline: 168 MW Abernathy, TX joint venture with Fluidstack (TeraWulf 51%): ~$9.5B over a 25-year lease, $1.3B Google credit support; $1.3B of JV secured notes followed in December
recentDevelopments.read: The Google-backstop template proved portable beyond Lake Mariner — and nine months later the position was sold at a ~20% IRR, showing the paper itself is liquid.

recentDevelopments.headline: Prices $3.2B of 7.75% senior secured notes due 2030 at subsidiary WULF Compute LLC (Morgan Stanley sole bookrunner) to fund the Lake Mariner HPC buildout — secured by the Fluidstack leases and a pre-completion Google warrant pledge
recentDevelopments.read: Project-finance-style debt against contracted leases — the capital structure the whole landlord model depends on, at a coupon that shows lenders still price execution risk.

recentDevelopments.headline: Fluidstack expands with the 160 MW CB-5 lease four days after the initial 200+ MW agreements — Lake Mariner Fluidstack total >360 MW, $6.7B contracted (~$16B with extensions); Google backstop rises to $3.2B, warrants to ~14% pro forma
recentDevelopments.read: The August 2025 week that re-rated the company: two leases, a Google guarantee, and a stock that gained a third in a day. Google's economics — downside protection via backstop, upside via penny warrants — reveal how AI-buildout credit actually gets underwritten.

recentDevelopments.headline: Acquires Beowulf Electricity & Data — CEO Prager's related-party services entity (~$52.4M base consideration, 94 employees internalized)
recentDevelopments.read: Partial remediation of the governance critique at the center of the 2024 Grizzly/Hunterbrook short reports (>$100M of fees alleged to Prager-affiliated entities) — by buying the CEO's own service company.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess the business model is credit arbitrage on power scarcity: TeraWulf converts brownfield megawatts into long take-or-pay leases signed by thinly-capitalized AI intermediaries, then makes the paper bankable with third-party credit enhancement — Google's amortizing backstops (~$4.5B across the Fluidstack chain) and Anthropic's investment-grade-supported lease. Basis: SEC 8-K backstop mechanics (Google must assume the lease on Fluidstack default, subject to triggers), and the $3.2B project notes secured against exactly that support. The ~14% of pro forma equity granted to Google is the disclosed price of bankability.

(High confidence) We assess the July 2026 Anthropic lease materially de-risked the tenant chain. Basis: trade press had mapped Anthropic's $50B Fluidstack program onto TeraWulf's sites in Nov 2025; the direct 20-year lease made the end-tenant explicit and shifted concentration from a private middleman toward a frontier lab with investment-grade support — better credit, still narrow (two counterparty chains carry ~everything).

(High confidence) We assess GAAP results will remain structurally misleading in both directions while warrants are outstanding. Basis: $755.7M of the Q2 2026 loss was warrant mark-to-market that rises when the stock rises; MarketBeat logs six straight EPS misses against a Strong Buy consensus and a ~$36.64 average target vs ~$15.64 price. Anyone reading this company through EPS is reading the wrong line — contracted MW energized on schedule is the metric.

(Moderate confidence) We assess brownfield repeatability — not Lake Mariner — is the open execution question. Basis: Lake Mariner's ~$9.1M per critical-IT MW sits below Bernstein's revised $10–12M industry band, but Bernstein expects Kentucky at the high end, and Data Center Frontier flags 'minimal procurement buffer' on the 2H 2027 Anthropic schedule with transformers/switchgear/chillers as choke points; a $150M unplanned tenant fit-out contribution already appeared in the July 2026 lease amendments.

(Moderate confidence) We assess a residual governance discount persists by design of the ownership structure. Basis: the 2024 Grizzly and Hunterbrook short reports (related-party fees, zero-carbon branding disputes), the CEO's $39.4M 2025 compensation against a $661M loss year, a 9-member board with only 5 independents including a Prager family member, and a diluted share count (~613M) 23% above basic — partially remediated by the Beowulf E&D internalization, never fully resolved. Collection gap: no securities class action was ever filed; the 2024 law-firm investigations produced none that independent sources record.

relationships.note: ~$4.5B of lease credit backstops bought with warrants now ~14% of the company pro forma.
relationships.context:
Google provides amortizing credit backstops across TeraWulf's Fluidstack lease chain — $3.2B behind the Lake Mariner leases (378 MW, ~$6.7B contracted, up to ~$16B with extensions) plus $1.3B behind the 168 MW Abernathy, TX JV — with SEC 8-K mechanics obliging Google to assume the lease on Fluidstack default. The warrants Google received equal ~14% of pro forma equity: the disclosed price of bankability, and the paper the $3.2B of 7.75% WULF Compute notes are secured against.

The dossier's frame: TeraWulf is credit arbitrage on power scarcity — brownfield megawatts converted into 10-20-year take-or-pay leases with thinly capitalized AI intermediaries, made bankable by Google's investment-grade support (and Anthropic's investment-grade-supported 401 MW/~$19B Hawesville lease).
